- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment index (0–1) into forecast by 15–30% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.80” peaks followed by “0.27” drops, model tends to overreact; apply a 10–15% downward correction after such sentiment shifts.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is “0.00” for 3+ consecutive days — treat as bearish trap; forecast should be 2–4% below historical mean for next 5 days.
